title: Build a complete prediction
target: Connect net force, velocity change, and final position in one model.
criteria: Connect force, acceleration and position consistently.
Show quantities and units at every stage.
Explain the assumptions and limits of the prediction.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: A 4 kg rover has constant forces 26 N right and 10 N left. What is acceleration?
cpa.guide: Net force = 16 N right; divide by 4 kg.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A rover starts from rest with acceleration +4 m/s² for 3 s. What is final velocity?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A rover starts from rest with constant acceleration 4 m/s² for 3 s. What is displacement?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: The same 18 m rightward displacement begins at x = −7 m. What is final position?
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Which assumptions support predicting motion from a constant net force using a = F_net/m?
options: Fixed mass, constant net force over the interval, and an inertial reference frame.
Any changing mass and force with no adjustment.
Only that the object has a name.
cpa.guide: These conditions support constant acceleration; initial conditions are also needed for the motion prediction.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: The motor weakens halfway through the modeled interval. What should happen to a prediction based on constant net force?
options: Keep the original prediction as exact regardless of evidence.
Set all previous displacement to zero.
Revise the force model and calculate the intervals consistently.
cpa.guide: A changed force changes acceleration; update the assumptions and resulting motion.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Select a claim supported by the stated evidence and assumptions.
